key_gap: vs baseline: the human's decisive move was cushioning the binding n=1 uncertainty (surge factor — a single non-instrumented observation, ±25%) to reach 115 kN/m², and the non-routed v5 AI lost exactly there: it priced the one-sided tail against a $230k premium on EV grounds (1% × $3.5M = $35k < $230k), chose 92 kN/m², and the graded 93 kN/m² event damaged it (plate yield ≈ $340k). The routed run converts the human's winning move into load-bearing structure: the m038 contract's margin-quantified flip-point table (92 flips at any single-factor ≈ 2σ miss; 115 flips only at a joint miss), the P1 provenance audit (surge = n=1 observation adverse to the cheap option — the tell it is real), the m003 inversion gate (6 ranked failure categories), and P3 pricing the 92-failure branch ($340k–3.5M). Residual shared gap: tourism growth +60% and the ±25% surge bound are asserted, not measured; the wind-event coincidence is unmodeled.
learning_signal: On estimate/guarantee signatures whose margin chain contains a single-observation (n=1) error factor, EV arithmetic systematically underweights the one-sided tail: the non-routed run discounted a ~1% joint event against the premium and lost the style's home turf. The margin-quantified contract — 'how wrong must each estimate be before the decision flips?' — makes the binding factor the sizing object: the design must cover the error in the margin's own inputs, not just the nominal numbers, and a one-sided error structure (a survey can only understate) earns a one-sided margin. The cushion is then priced against the failure it retires (92→115 costs $230k vs a $340k–3.5M tail — the cheapest item in the budget), not EV-discounted as a premium.
suggested_improvement: Install the m038 first-class contract as: (1) margin-quantified — a per-factor flip-point table ('how wrong before the decision flips'), (2) binding-uncertainty audit — n=1 / single-observation factors get the cushion instead of a sensitivity note, with a P1 who-benefits check (a factor adverse to the cheap option is the tell it is real), (3) over-conservatism check — opportunity cost of the cushion priced against the failure it retires, (4) derating — factors backed by evidence are not inflated; reserve the over-conservatism gate for capped-downside cases. Pair with the m003 inversion gate on guarantee goals (ranked failure categories before selection) and P3 (price the under-cushioned branch before DO).

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-margin human baseline declined to bid on a blanket 2× margin ($1.04M cost basis, ≈ 24-week schedule) against a contract whose true tail is ±20% (reference class, 90% of cases; worst plausible $660k/11.5 wk) and whose downside is contractually capped at ≈ $80–120k — forgoing ≈ $165k now and ≈ $2M/5yr of repeat + vendor-list business to 'avoid' a capped $120k loss. The non-routed v5 AI escaped by calibrating ($700k/11.5 wk), but the routed run makes the escape structural: the m038 contract's over-conservatism check + derating (2× → ≈ 17% cost margin + 2-wk schedule buffer) gate-checks the style's own failure mode in-frame, the m007 ruin screen proves no ruin path (max loss $120k < $165k expected profit — the cap is the true ruin bound), m023 prices the forgone alternative at ≈ $2M/5yr, m019 audits the competitor's under-margined $610k baseline, and m088 pre-commits the delivery buffers. Residual shared gap: cost beyond the ±20% tail (10% of cases) is absorbed by the caps only if the client honors them (litigation risk unmodeled).
learning_signal: On adversarial/high_stakes decide signatures with a contractually capped downside, margin is a derated calibration, not a blanket factor: size it from (a) the reference-class base rate (±20%, 90% of cases), (b) the named-risk worst case ($660k/11.5 wk), and (c) the contract cap as the true ruin bound (≈ $120k). A blanket 2× margin on top of a capped downside is taxed twice — it forfeits an uncapped upside that never needed insuring (≈ 20× overpay: $2M/5yr foregone to avoid ≤ $120k). The derating test: 'does the demanded margin cost more than the risk it retires?' — if yes, derate to evidence-based sizing and pre-commit the buffers that actually win (schedule + scope-change protocol) rather than the one that kills the bid (2× cost).
suggested_improvement: Add to the m038 contract a derating clause: when the downside is contractually capped, (1) compute the true ruin bound from the contract (exit clause, penalty cap) and compare it against the uncapped upside (repeat contracts, market entry) before choosing any factor, (2) derive the margin from the reference class (m097) + named-risk worst case instead of a blanket multiplier, (3) run the 'margin costs more than the risk' test (m023) and derate if positive, (4) convert the freed margin into pre-committed operational buffers (m088: schedule slack, scope-change protocol). Extend the m007 ruin-screen ordering: on capped-loss contracts the floor/Kelly line becomes a cap-vs-upside asymmetry check, and the ruin question is 'can the contract lose us more than X?', not 'what is the worst statistical case?'
